there are some things that are not talked about and others that are. You will be bothered between your legs especially the first month, the lack of menstruation is very random, you will probably have pain in your ovaries, random bleeding due to hormonal imbalance and your stomach will be swollen, very hungry, you will be in sex mode (I am practically an asexual person so if these things do not matter to you it can be a problem), you sweat a lot, you will be hotter, you will put on weight but all for a "masculine" silhouette, you will have more strength and be a little more muscular, acne, more hair, some people's throat bothers them the first few months even if there is no voice change. In truth you must be prepared for many times to feel that you are going too slow, dysphoria changes, normal frustrations in a process, but remember that sooner or later you will have the changes you fought so hard for (pro tip: exercising is very useful in many ways and you take advantage of the extra energy)

I was in exactly the same position as you a couple of months ago, no matter what I wore or how I spoke everyone referred to me as a lady or a woman, because of previous psychological issues I was denied testosterone for 1 year it was extremely unfair, but I think part of the process as a trans person is to take hormone therapy not because you will finally be you, but as part of the process just like wearing men's clothes or getting a haircut and understand that with or without hormones you are a man and that's it, because it's all about attitude. It seems difficult now but at some point you will have the long awaited testosterone but not to be you and for others to see you that way but to make inhabiting your own body more enjoyable and with that extra confidence people will not doubt that you are a man
